metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Wyoming (2026): Rules & Exemptions

description: Wyoming has a statewide sales tax, but gold/silver legal-tender coins and investment-grade bullion are fully exempt. Jewelry is taxable; noncovered items are taxed.

What's covered by the exemption
Gold/silver legal-tender and investment-grade bullion
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Wyoming.
Is bullion sales-tax exempt in Wyoming?
+
Yes. Wyoming fully exempts gold and silver investment-grade bullion from sales tax under the statewide rule.
Are legal-tender gold and silver coins taxed in Wyoming?
+
No. Gold and silver legal-tender style coins treated as investment items are exempt in Wyoming.
Are numismatic coins taxable in Wyoming?
+
It depends. Numismatic items are conditional and are often exempt if they qualify as bullion or legal tender under Wyoming’s treatment.
Is jewelry taxed in Wyoming even if it’s precious metal?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable in Wyoming; the exemption applies to covered bullion and certain qualifying coins, not jewelry.
